verdict.root_cause: paymentservice's request path was healthy throughout - charges completed sub-millisecond with no error lines [tr_3dd82d1dd4a4] and checkoutservice recorded successful payments with advancing offsets [tr_42e1086a8f96], errors at flat zero [tr_84bf1c40f945]. What is actually wrong is paymentservice's telemetry: platform-automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT to http://127.0.0.1:4317 about five minutes before onset and left it applied [tr_d69ff6028ed5], pointing span export at loopback where no collector listens. The span-derived calls_total series for paymentservice is absent from Prometheus in both incident and baseline windows [tr_38a280485320], so the alert at 09:33:45 fired on missing telemetry rather than on failing requests. Reverting the endpoint value restores span delivery and the derived metrics.
verdict.reasoning: No specialist found a failing request anywhere: paymentservice logs are all info-level success pairs bracketing the marker, checkoutservice logs show payment succeeding end to end, and checkoutservice error ratio is zero for all 128 incident samples. The only anomaly with a mechanism is the exporter endpoint pointed at loopback five minutes before onset, and the only observed defect is the total absence of paymentservice's span-derived metric series. The wrong value (a loopback address for a remote collector) is itself the failure mode - telemetry is discarded because the address is wrong - which makes this bad_config rather than a deploy or exhaustion.
open_questions: The trace query that found paymentservice spans intact covered 21:33-03:33, six hours before onset, so it does not test whether export was working after the 09:27 edit; the loopback hypothesis is inferred, not directly observed at incident time.
Two earlier identical set/revert cycles did not produce this onset [tr_d69ff6028ed5], so either a second condition coincided or the alert threshold was reached only this time - unexplained.
No request-rate, latency, CPU, memory or saturation data was retrieved for paymentservice [tr_38a280485320], so a real but silent degradation cannot be fully excluded.
checkoutservice's baseline half-hour averaged ~15% errors that vanished at the window boundary [tr_84bf1c40f945]; that transition is unexplained and may indicate an earlier, separate fault.
The paymentservice hostname change mid-window [tr_3dd82d1dd4a4] suggests a pod replacement whose timing was never dated.

alternatives.root_cause: The shippingservice-to-quoteservice hop was slow and dragged checkout latency, with paymentservice merely the alerting bystander.
alternatives.why_not: The degrading hop was flagged only in traces from a window six hours before onset, cost 5-8ms, and no specialist observed latency or errors on the checkout path during the incident window.

alternatives.root_cause: paymentservice was genuinely degraded around 09:33:45 and the metric gap plus log silence reflect a brief stall, not a telemetry misconfiguration.
alternatives.why_not: The ~3.5s log gap at the marker is matched by longer quiet gaps later in the same window, and the metric series is missing in the baseline too, so neither signal is anomalous at onset.

proposal.expected_effect: No action taken, so nothing should change: paymentservice charge pairs stay info-level and sub-millisecond, checkoutservice error ratio stays flat at zero, and the paymentservice calls_total series stays absent from Prometheus. I decline revert_config even though its preconditions are met, because the effect it is supposed to produce cannot be expected: calls_total is equally empty in the 09:03-09:35 baseline, most of which followed the 04:32 revert to the correct endpoint [tr_38a280485320][tr_d69ff6028ed5], and spans were in fact being delivered with paymentservice Charge spans present in every trace [tr_0076d8bf5cfd]. The likely cause is that the metric does not exist under the queried name/label set - a span-metrics or recording-rule problem in the telemetry pipeline, which no permitted action reaches. Next step is a query, not a change: re-run the trace query over 09:27-09:35 and check calls_total under any label set.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if a trace query scoped to 09:27-09:35 shows paymentservice spans absent while 09:03-09:27 shows them present, dating export loss to the edit and making revert_config correct; or if calls_total is found under a different label set with a real excursion at 09:33:45. Note that with the derived series absent, a successful revert would have no metric to confirm it - part of why I withhold it.
proposal.risk: Abstention leaves the loopback endpoint applied, so if export really is broken after 09:27 the telemetry blind spot on paymentservice persists and a silent degradation could go unseen - no rate, latency, CPU or saturation data was ever retrieved [tr_38a280485320]. It also leaves the alert able to re-fire on missing telemetry.
proposal.blast_radius: None now. Had revert_config been run, paymentservice would be recreated, with checkoutservice seeing a brief connection reset and frontend seeing it through checkout.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A critical alert on paymentservice with checkout and frontend downstream is not dismissible, and no open incident could account for it. Nothing in the single seed alert points to a specific fault class yet.
